resources.string: An illustration of one normal cranial nerve reflex, not a survey of all cranial nerves or a guide to testing or diagnosis. Nerve routes are simplified; motion and timing are not to scale.
Light enters one eye through its pupil and reaches the retina. Retinal nerve cells signal the increase in light.
The optic nerve (cranial nerve II) carries the signal toward the brain. Some fibers cross at the optic chiasm and others stay on the same side, so input reaches the pretectum on both sides.
The midbrain relays to both sides
In the midbrain, the pretectum relays the light signal to the paired Edinger-Westphal nuclei, which send motor signals toward the eyes.
Motor signals return to both eyes
Parasympathetic signals travel in each oculomotor nerve (cranial nerve III) to the ciliary ganglion, then along short ciliary nerves to the iris sphincter.

The iris sphincters contract, narrowing both pupils. Narrowing in the lit eye is the direct response; narrowing in the other eye is the consensual response. Smaller pupils admit less light to the retina, one part of light adaptation.
